answer: A bonded identity vault resists Sybils by making each agent lock a refundable stake before it can trade. The vault releases the stake only after a clean record; proven fraud forfeits it. An attacker creating many fake identities must fund a separate stake for each, so the cost scales linearly with the number of fakes, while honest agents recover theirs. Even at the nadir of trust, when new identities are most suspect, the delta between a real participant and a cheap fake is the stake at risk: fakes become expensive, and honest participation stays cheap.
